headerDisplay: Control Samsung air conditioners from the Home app, Siri and your HomePod. Connect to SmartThings above, then pick which extras to show.

pollInterval.title: Refresh every (seconds)
pollInterval.description: How often Paperclip reads the AC from SmartThings. Changes you make in HomeKit are sent immediately either way.

optionalModeSwitches.title: Samsung extra modes to show as switches
optionalModeSwitches.description: Only modes your unit supports are added. The settings page above lists your unit's modes.

dryModeSwitch.title: Dry (dehumidify) switch
dryModeSwitch.description: HomeKit has no dry mode, so it gets its own switch. Turning it off returns the AC to its previous mode.

humiditySensor.title: Humidity sensor
humiditySensor.description: Shows the room humidity your AC measures (if it has a sensor).

displaySwitch.title: Display light switch
displaySwitch.description: Turns the temperature display on the indoor unit on or off.

swingMode.title: Swing direction when you turn swing on

excludeDevices.title: Hide these air conditioners
excludeDevices.description: Names or SmartThings device IDs (shown in the Homebridge log) to leave out of HomeKit.

removeStaleAccessories.title: Remove ACs that are deleted from SmartThings

clientId.title: OAuth Client ID
clientId.description: Only for manual setups. The settings page above normally stores this for you.

refreshToken.title: OAuth Refresh Token
refreshToken.description: Used once; after that Paperclip keeps the rotated token in its own file.

accessToken.title: Personal access token (testing only)
accessToken.description: SmartThings tokens stop working 24 hours after you create them. Use the setup above instead.

layout.title: HomeKit extras
layout.description: Everything here is optional and only appears if your unit supports it.
